info.title: Gateway SMS
info.description:
The Gateway SMS API by Openapi provides a robust and scalable solution for integrating professional SMS messaging into your applications. Our service is designed to handle high volumes of messages with precision, offering dedicated endpoints for specific regions like Italy and Spain, as well as a Worldwide endpoint for global reach.

Each request undergoes a rigorous validation process that includes syntax checking for **E.164 formats**, character encoding detection (GSM-7 or UCS-2), and automatic segmentation for long messages. We prioritize security and compliance: the system automatically scans content for forbidden words to prevent abuse and ensures that all messages comply with legal requirements.

Developers can benefit from advanced features such as **dryRun** for testing without incurring costs, and real-time Webhook callbacks that provide immediate updates on delivery status. Messages have a maximum **expiration time** of **48 hours**; if a message cannot be delivered within this window, its status will change to EXPIRED. Billing is transparent and dynamic; while regional messages have fixed rates, worldwide delivery costs are calculated post-sending to ensure the best market price. Please note that maintaining a minimum credit balance is required for worldwide operations, and strict penalties apply for policy violations to ensure the highest quality of service for all users.

##### 🆔 Alias Names

Aliases must be registered in advance via the **POST /senders/alias** endpoint and **approved** before they can be used for sending. For professional messaging in compliance with local regulations (specifically for **Italy**), sending messages is only permitted for **registered companies** that have completed their business verification.

 New aliases are subject to verification and approval by Openapi and mobile operators. **If messages are not delivered during an initial testing phase, please contact us so we can run specific checks on the requests.** Once validated, the alias will be associated with the customer and can be used regularly without service interruptions.

##### 🧪 Sandbox Environment

The Sandbox environment (test.sms.openapi.com) lets you test the whole integration without real deliveries. Aliases are required in Sandbox too: there is no shared or default alias so every message must use an alias registered by your account for the destination country, otherwise the request is rejected, even with **dryRun** enabled.

In Sandbox the registration is **approved immediately** (state **APPROVED**): it is not reviewed, it is not submitted to the mobile operators or to the authorities, and it does not activate anything in Production. 

Sandbox and Production are separate: an alias registered in Sandbox cannot be used in Production, where it must be registered again and goes through the full review.

##### ✅ Content Validation Whitelist

If you need to bypass the message content validation for particular business reasons (e.g. legitimate use of otherwise filtered words), you can contact our support and request to be added to the **whitelist**. Each request is subject to **internal review and approval**; once approved, messages sent with your whitelisted sender skip the content validation filters. All other compliance rules still apply.

##### ⚠️ WARNING: Content Restrictions

**Sandbox Environment**: The Sandbox environment (test.sms.openapi.com) has no restrictions on the message content, allowing developers to test integration freely. **Please note that messages sent in the Sandbox environment will not be actually delivered.**

**Production Environment**: The Production environment (sms.openapi.com) implements strict automated scanning for forbidden words. Sending messages with prohibited content in Production without using the **dryRun** option for pre-verification will lead to immediate blocking and the user being placed on a blocklist with associated penalties.

##### 🚫 WARNING: Anti-spam Policy

To protect the quality of the service and comply with mobile operator requirements, traffic is monitored for spam-like patterns. Sending traffic that matches any of the following thresholds is considered a policy violation and may lead to the blocking of the traffic and of the account, with the associated penalties:

- **Per-recipient frequency**: more than **20 messages** sent to the same recipient within **60 minutes**.
- **Duplicate messages**: more than **6 messages** with identical content sent to the same recipient within **60 minutes**.

tags.name: Messages
tags.description: Operations for sending and retrieving SMS messages.

SendMessageRequest.description: Request body for sending a new SMS message.

sender.description: The message sender. Must be a sender already registered via POST /senders and APPROVED for the destination country. Sending with an unregistered or unapproved sender is rejected.

recipient.description: The recipient's number in international E.164 format.

message.description: The text of the message to be sent. Segmentation is handled automatically. GSM-7 encoding allows up to 160 characters per part (153 if multi-part), while UCS-2 allows up to 70 characters (67 if multi-part).
message.example: Hello! This is a test message.

SendOTPRequest.description: Request body for sending an OTP verification message.

recipient.description: The recipient's number in international E.164 format.

alphanumeric.description: If set to **true**, the generated OTP will be alphanumeric. If **false** (default), it will be purely numeric.

length.description: The length of the OTP code (min 4, max 10).

cacheSeconds.description: The number of seconds within which the same OTP code will be reused for the same recipient (max 600).

dryRun.description: If set to **true**, the request is validated and calculated, but the message is not actually sent.

failOnMultipleMessages.description: If set to **true**, the request will fail if the message text exceeds the length of a single SMS part.

CallbackOptions.description: This is our standardized OpenAPI callback system. It enables the configuration of parameters for receiving notifications about status updates of asynchronous requests to this endpoint.

method.description: Specify the callback method. When set to **POST**, a standard HTTP POST request will be initiated with the Content-Type header set to application/x-www-form-urlencoded. The JSON data will be encoded into a key-value pair named data (customizable using the field parameter) within the request body. If the method is set to **JSON**, a direct HTTP POST request will be made with the Content-Type header set to application/json. The raw JSON data will be directly inserted into the request body without any encoding.

field.description: This parameter works in conjunction with the **method** parameter set to **POST**. When provided as a string, it determines the name of the parameter that will be sent in the POST request.

url.description: A valid URL capable of handling POST requests must be entered into this parameter. For endpoints requiring authentication, the **headers** parameter can be used to specify **basic auth** or **bearer auth**. The maximum timeout is 30 seconds. If **retry** is set, the system will retry up to **retry** times until a 200 status code is received.

retry.description: The maximum number of attempts is defined by the **retry** parameter. If the maximum number of attempts is reached without a successful status code (e.g., 200 OK), the request is considered a final failure. A time interval is often introduced between attempts to avoid overloading the server. This interval may increase exponentially with each attempt to reduce the impact on an overloaded server. The **retry** parameter is configured to retry the request only in case of specific status codes, typically those indicating temporary errors (e.g., 502, 503) or network issues.

headers.description: A collection of HTTP headers to be sent with the request. Each header is defined as a key-value pair. Headers can be used for various purposes, including authentication, content negotiation, and custom metadata. Each key is limited to 256 characters, each value must be a string, and the serialized headers object must not exceed 256 bytes in total. These headers are sent as real HTTP headers of the callback request.

custom.description: This object can be populated with any additional data you wish to include in the callback response. This data will be accessible within the **custom** parameter of the callback function. You can use this to store and retrieve any relevant information that you need for your application.

OTPOptions.description: Configuration used for the OTP generation.

id.description: The unique ID of the message in our system.

username.description: Username of the account that sent the message.

state.description: The current state of the message. The maximum expiration time for delivery attempts is 48 hours. If a message cannot be delivered within this window, its status will change to EXPIRED.

sender.description: The sender used for the delivery.

internationalPrefix.description: The international prefix of the recipient's number.

countryCode.description: The ISO country code of the recipient.

message.description: The text of the sent message.

encoding.description: The encoding detected for the message.

charactersCount.description: The number of characters calculated according to the encoding rules.

messageCount.description: The number of SMS segments required to send the message.

price.description: The cost per single SMS part. For WW messages, this is initially 0 and updated after provider acceptance.

totalPrice.description: The total cost of the message (price * messageCount). For WW messages, this is initially 0 and updated after provider acceptance.

blocklisted.description: Indicates if the message was blocked due to forbidden content.

blocklistedReason.description: The reason why the message was blocklisted (if applicable).

isOtp.description: Indicates if the message is an OTP.

otp.description: The generated OTP code (only present for OTP requests).

code.description: An internal error code for quick problem identification.

message.description: A clear description of the error.

Sender.description: Represent a message sender registered by a user.

state.description: The current state of the sender registration. **PATCH_REQUIRED** means the registration data must be corrected or completed via PATCH /senders/{id}: a sender in this state cannot send messages until it is approved again.

rejectReason.description: Why the registration was rejected. Present only on senders in **REJECTED** state, and only when the reviewer provided a reason.
rejectReason.example: The alias is generic and does not refer to your company or to one of its brands.

registrationData.description: The registration data currently stored for this sender. The set of fields depends on the country: see the country schemas of RegisterSenderRequest. Uploaded documents are not returned as files: each document field contains a reference object with the file metadata only (**filename**, **contentType**, **size** in bytes, **uploadedAt** in **Y-m-d H:i:s P** format).

patchRequest.description: History of the correction requests received by this sender, most recent first. The first item describes what has to be corrected while the sender is in PATCH_REQUIRED state; the following ones are the previous requests, kept for reference. Absent if the sender has never been flagged for correction.

reason.description: What the user has to correct or complete.
reason.example: The messageTemplate field does not match the declared traffic type.

requestedAt.description: When the correction was requested, in **Y-m-d H:i:s P** format.

createdAt.description: Registration date of the sender, in **Y-m-d H:i:s P** format.

updatedAt.description: Date of the last update of the sender registration, in **Y-m-d H:i:s P** format.

RegisterSenderRequest.description: Request body for registering a new alias. Every request requires the common fields defined in the base schema; depending on the selected country, additional fields may be required. Select the destination country from the list below to see its specific requirements.

SenderRegistrationBase.description: Common fields required for EVERY alias registration request, regardless of the destination country.

countryCode.description: The 2-character ISO alpha-2 code of the destination country. See the available country schemas for the supported values.

sender.description: The alias name to register. Between 3 and 11 characters, alphanumeric and spaces only, must contain at least one letter (cannot be purely numeric).

senderCompanyRelationship.description: The relationship between the alias name and the company (max 60 characters), e.g. company brand, trade name, product name.

companyWebsite.description: The website of the company registering the sender. Must be a valid URL.

industry.description: The industry of the company (max 50 characters).

trafficType.description: The type of SMS traffic that will be sent with this alias.

allOf.description: Italy: ALPHANUMERIC only. Registration is reserved to accounts of type **Company**: the account must be registered as a company and its company data must be verified. Accounts belonging to a private individual cannot register an Italian alias.

pec.description: Certified email address (PEC) of the company registering the sender. Required for Italian registrations: it is included in the data submitted to the competent authority.

allOf.description: United Kingdom: ALPHANUMERIC only, requires the additional fields **companyName**, **companyCountry** and **messageTemplate**, and supports **optOutMethod** (required only when **trafficType** is **promotional**).

companyName.description: The legal name of the company registering the alias (between 2 and 65 characters).

companyCountry.description: The country where the company registering the alias is based, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

optOutMethod.description: How recipients can opt out of receiving messages (max 100 characters), e.g. reply STOP. Required only when **trafficType** is **promotional**; for transactional traffic it can be omitted and defaults to **N/A**.

messageTemplate.description: A sample template of the messages that will be sent with this alias (max 2000 characters).
messageTemplate.example: Your order {orderId} has been shipped. Reply STOP to opt out.

allOf.description:
France: ALPHANUMERIC only, supports the additional field **optOutMethod** (required only when **trafficType** is **promotional**).

**Allowed send time window**: messages to French numbers can only be delivered between 08:00:00 and 21:30:00 UTC, every day of the week (Monday - Friday, Saturday, Sunday). A message sent outside this window is not rejected, but it might be routed to the next day, so the recipient could receive it with a significant delay compared to the request time.

optOutMethod.description: How recipients can opt out of receiving messages (max 100 characters), e.g. reply STOP. Required only when **trafficType** is **promotional**; for transactional traffic it can be omitted and defaults to **N/A**.

allOf.description: Ireland: ALPHANUMERIC only, no additional country-specific fields.
Switzerland: ALPHANUMERIC only, no additional country-specific fields.
Germany: ALPHANUMERIC only, no additional country-specific fields.
Austria: ALPHANUMERIC only, no additional country-specific fields.

Spain: ALPHANUMERIC only. The Spanish regulator CNMC requires the alias holder to be declared explicitly: the holder is the person or company the alias belongs to, which may be a third party and not the account holder. The declared details must match the ones in the two signed documents **esLoA** and **esResponsibleDeclaration**, or CNMC rejects the request. Field **companyWebsite** is the website of the alias holder, and field **senderCompanyRelationship** describes the relationship between the alias and the alias holder: when no registered name or domain matches the alias, that text reaches CNMC verbatim as the holder's justification for using it. The authorised representative of the alias holder is declared in the same way, in the **holderRepresentativeType** field and the ones that follow it: it is the party the holder authorises in the signed **esLoA**, and its details must match that document too.

senderCompanyRelationship.description: The relationship between the alias and the alias holder (max 60 characters), e.g. brand, trade name, product name. When no registered corporate name or registered domain matches the alias, this text is sent verbatim to CNMC as the holder's justification for using the alias, so it must describe the holder's own relationship to the alias, not the registering company's.

companyWebsite.description: The website of the alias holder, not necessarily of the company registering the sender. CNMC compliance checks whether the alias matches this domain to decide the relationship declared for the holder, so declaring a website that is not the holder's own can make the holder sign a declaration that does not apply to them. Must be a valid URL.

aliasHolderType.description: Whether the alias holder is a legal entity (**LE**) or a natural person (**NP**). It decides which fields are required: a legal entity declares its registered name in **aliasHolderName** and no surnames, a natural person declares their first name in **aliasHolderName** plus **holder1stSurname**.

aliasHolderTaxId.description: Tax identification number of the alias holder: the company tax number for a legal entity, the personal one (**NIF**, **NIE** or the equivalent in the holder country) for a natural person. Must match the number in the signed documents.

aliasHolderName.description: Registered company name when **aliasHolderType** is **LE**, first name when it is **NP**.

holder1stSurname.description: First surname of the alias holder. Required when **aliasHolderType** is **NP**, ignored when it is **LE**.

holder2ndSurname.description: Second surname of the alias holder, the Spanish **segundo apellido**. Optional, and only meaningful when **aliasHolderType** is **NP**: leave it out for a holder whose country does not use it.

holderMailingAddressStreetAvenue.description: Street name of the alias holder mailing address, without the street number.

holderMailingAddressStreetNumber.description: Street number of the alias holder mailing address. For a property with no street number, send the Spanish convention **S/N**.

holderMailingAddressPostalCode.description: Postal code of the alias holder mailing address.

holderMailingAddressCity.description: City of the alias holder mailing address. It completes the address written on the letterhead of the signed documents, so it must match the address declared in **esLoA** and **esResponsibleDeclaration**.

holderMailingAddressCountry.description: Country of the alias holder mailing address, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. It must match the **esLoA** template you signed: a holder in Spain signs the **IB_ES** template, a holder anywhere else signs the **IB_UK** one.

holderEmails.description: Contact email address of the alias holder. It is the holder's own address, not the one of its authorised representative, which goes in **representativeEmails**.

holderPhones.description: Contact phone number of the alias holder, in E.164 format. It is the holder's own number, not the one of its authorised representative, which goes in **representativePhones**.

holderRepresentativeType.description: Whether the authorised representative of the alias holder is a legal entity (**LE**) or a natural person (**NP**). The authorised representative is whoever acts on the alias holder's behalf in the signed documents, typically the natural person who signs them for the holder, and the details declared here must match what is written in those documents. This field decides which of the remaining representative fields are required: a natural person declares **representative1stSurname** and no company block, a legal entity declares its registered name in **representativeName** plus the four **legalEntityRepresentative** fields of the individual acting for it.

representativeTaxId.description: Tax identification number of the authorised representative: the company tax number when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**, the personal one when it is **NP**.

representativeName.description: Registered company name of the authorised representative when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**, first name when it is **NP**.

representative1stSurname.description: First surname of the authorised representative. Required when **holderRepresentativeType** is **NP**, ignored when it is **LE**.

representative2ndSurname.description: Second surname of the authorised representative, the Spanish **segundo apellido**. Optional, and only meaningful when **holderRepresentativeType** is **NP**: leave it out for a representative whose country does not use it.

representativeEmails.description: Contact email address of the authorised representative.

representativePhones.description: Contact phone number of the authorised representative, in E.164 format.

legalEntityRepresentativeTaxId.description: Tax identification number of the individual acting for the authorised representative. Required when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**, ignored when it is **NP**.

legalEntityRepresentativeName.description: First name of the individual acting for the authorised representative. Required when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**, ignored when it is **NP**.

legalEntityRepresentative1stSurname.description: First surname of the individual acting for the authorised representative. Required when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**, ignored when it is **NP**.

legalEntityRepresentative2ndSurname.description: Second surname of the individual acting for the authorised representative. Optional, and only meaningful when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**.

esLoA.description:
Letter of Authorisation (**Carta de Autorización**), signed by the alias holder, authorising the mobile aggregator to act as its representative before the Spanish regulator CNMC. Base64 encoded PDF file, max 5 MB decoded.

There are four templates, one per case. Which one you need depends on two things: whether the alias holder is an individual or a company, and whether the holder is in Spain or outside it.

- **Individual in Spain** — resident in Spain, or with legal residence in Spain: [download](https://storage.googleapis.com/docs-openapi-it-bucket/smsv2/documents/ES/LOA_Spanish_natural_person_or_person_with_legal_residence_in_Spain_IB_ES_signed.pdf)
- **Company in Spain** — registered in Spain: [download](https://storage.googleapis.com/docs-openapi-it-bucket/smsv2/documents/ES/LOA_Spanish_Legal_Entity_IB_ES_signed.pdf)
- **Individual outside Spain** — [download](https://storage.googleapis.com/docs-openapi-it-bucket/smsv2/documents/ES/LOA_Foreign_Individual_IB_UK_signed.pdf)
- **Company outside Spain** — [download](https://storage.googleapis.com/docs-openapi-it-bucket/smsv2/documents/ES/LOA_Foreign_Legal_Entity_IB_UK_signed.pdf)

Each template names a different authorised representative, so signing the wrong one gets the request rejected by CNMC.

**How to fill it in**: the document is in Spanish, it is two pages long, and every blank line has to be completed.

- **Place and date** of signature, in the line that opens the document: **En [place] a [day] de [month] de [year]**. The month is written in Spanish, in words.
- **Who signs**: full name, then the identification the template asks for. The Spanish individual template asks for the **DNI** of a Spanish citizen, or the identity document or residence permit number of a foreign citizen with legal residence in Spain, plus the tax identification number; fill in only the one that applies to you and leave the other blank. The Spanish company template asks only for the identity document number of the signer. Both templates for a holder outside Spain also ask for the nationality of the signer and for the country whose law gives them legal capacity.
- **Individual templates**: the holder signs in their own name as a self-employed professional (**persona trabajadora autónoma**) and declares their professional address. There is no company block. The template for a holder outside Spain also asks for the country whose law governs that self-employed status.
- **Company templates**: the signer is the legal representative of the holder and declares the registered name of the company, its registered address, its tax identification number and its entry in the commercial registry — registry office and page for a company in Spain, the equivalent register of the holder country otherwise. The template for a company outside Spain also asks for the law the company was incorporated under, which for a company in Spain is already printed. The Spanish template also asks for the type of representation, listed in the footnote: **administrador**, **consejero delegado**, **apoderado**, or a legal representative other than those.
- **Authorised representative block** (**AUTORIZO A**) and the list of powers that follows it: already completed in the template. Leave both exactly as they are.
- **Final declaration**: the name of the signer has to be repeated in the closing paragraph **Yo, [name], declaro expresamente...**, where they state that the declared data is true.
- **Signature**: the holder signs at the end of the document, under **Firma del Titular**, on the left. The signature already printed next to it, under **Firma del Representante Autorizado**, is the one of the authorised representative: leave it as it is.

**Examples**. The plain text is the wording already printed in the template: leave it as it is. Only the parts in bold between square brackets are yours to fill in, and the square brackets are not to be typed.

**Individual in Spain**:

> En **[Madrid]** a **[12]** de **[marzo]** de **[2026]**
>
> Por la presente, yo, **[María García López]**, de nacionalidad **[española]**, mayor de edad, con DNI **[12345678Z]** / documento de identidad / permiso de residencia número ____, y número de identificación fiscal **[12345678Z]**, en mi propio nombre y derecho como persona trabajadora autónoma, con domicilio profesional en **[Calle Gran Vía 28, 28013 Madrid]** (en adelante, el Titular),

In that example the request would carry:

- **aliasHolderType**: NP
- **aliasHolderName**: María
- **holder1stSurname**: García
- **holder2ndSurname**: López
- **aliasHolderTaxId**: 12345678Z
- **holderMailingAddressStreetAvenue**: Calle Gran Vía
- **holderMailingAddressStreetNumber**: 28
- **holderMailingAddressPostalCode**: 28013
- **holderMailingAddressCountry**: ES

**Company in Spain**:

> Por la presente, yo, **[Juan Pérez Ruiz]**, mayor de edad, con documento de identidad número **[87654321X]**, en nombre y representación de **[EJEMPLO COMERCIAL, S.L.]**, con domicilio en **[Calle Gran Vía 28, 28013 Madrid]** y número de identificación fiscal **[B12345678]**, inscrita en el Registro Mercantil de **[Madrid]** en la hoja **[M-123456]**, como **[administrador]** con capacidad y facultades suficientes para suscribir el presente acto, entidad constituida conforme a la legislación española, (en adelante, el Titular)

In that example the request would carry:

- **aliasHolderType**: LE
- **aliasHolderName**: EJEMPLO COMERCIAL, S.L.
- **aliasHolderTaxId**: B12345678
- **holderMailingAddressStreetAvenue**: Calle Gran Vía
- **holderMailingAddressStreetNumber**: 28
- **holderMailingAddressPostalCode**: 28013
- **holderMailingAddressCountry**: ES

**Individual outside Spain**, whose template also asks for the nationality and for the countries whose law applies:

> Por la presente, yo, **[Marco Rossi]**, de nacionalidad **[italiana]**, mayor de edad y con capacidad suficiente de acuerdo con las leyes de **[Italia]**, con número de identificación fiscal / documento de identidad número **[RSSMRC80A01H501U]**, en mi propio nombre y derecho como persona trabajadora autónoma conforme a la legislación de **[Italia]**, con domicilio profesional en **[Via Roma 10, 00184 Roma]** (en adelante, el Titular),

**Company outside Spain**, whose template replaces the Spanish commercial registry with the equivalent register of the holder country and asks for no type of representation:

> Por la presente, yo, **[Marco Rossi]**, de nacionalidad **[italiana]**, mayor de edad y con capacidad suficiente de acuerdo con las leyes de **[Italia]**, con documento de identidad número / número de identificación fiscal **[RSSMRC80A01H501U]**, en nombre y representación de **[ESEMPIO COMMERCIALE S.R.L.]**, entidad constituida conforme a la legislación de **[Italia]**, con domicilio en **[Via Roma 10, 00184 Roma]**, y número de identificación fiscal **[12345678901]**, inscrita en el Registro Mercantil (o Registro análogo de su nacionalidad) **[Registro delle Imprese di Roma, n. RM-1234567]**, como representante legal con capacidad y facultades suficientes...

For those two the request would carry **holderMailingAddressCountry**: IT, which is what makes the **IB_UK** template the right one.

The name, tax identification number and address written here must match **aliasHolderName**, **aliasHolderTaxId** and the holder mailing address fields sent in this request: CNMC compares them and rejects the request when they differ. In the same way, the representative fields sent in this request — **holderRepresentativeType**, **representativeTaxId**, **representativeName**, **representative1stSurname**, **representative2ndSurname** and, when the representative is a legal entity, the four **legalEntityRepresentative** fields — must match whoever signs this document on the holder's behalf, the individual named in the opening paragraph **Por la presente, yo, [name]...**, not the **AUTORIZO A** block, which stays printed in the template and is not to be edited.

esResponsibleDeclaration.description:
Responsible declaration (**Declaración responsable**) of the alias holder, signed by the holder. Base64 encoded PDF file, max 5 MB decoded.

There are four templates, one per case. Which one you need depends on two things.

First, whether the alias holder is an individual or a company. Second, whether the alias can be traced to an official registry:

- **With connection** — the alias matches, or is a shortening or an extension of, the holder's registered corporate name, or of a registered internet domain given as the company website.
- **Without connection** — the alias is only used in fact in the course of business, with no registry entry backing it.

The four templates:

- **Individual, with connection** — [download](https://storage.googleapis.com/docs-openapi-it-bucket/smsv2/documents/ES/ES_Responsible_Declaration_of_the_Alias_Holder_with_Connection_to_Official_Registries_natural_person.pdf)
- **Company, with connection** — [download](https://storage.googleapis.com/docs-openapi-it-bucket/smsv2/documents/ES/ES_Responsible_Declaration_of_the_Alias_Holder_with_Connection_to_Official_Registries_legal_entity.pdf)
- **Individual, without connection** — [download](https://storage.googleapis.com/docs-openapi-it-bucket/smsv2/documents/ES/ES_Responsible_Declaration_of_the_Alias_Holder_without_Connection_to_Official_Registries_natural_person.pdf)
- **Company, without connection** — [download](https://storage.googleapis.com/docs-openapi-it-bucket/smsv2/documents/ES/ES_Responsible_Declaration_of_the_Alias_Holder_without_Connection_to_Official_Registries_legal_entity.pdf)

The link between the alias and its holder is derived from the registration data and declared to CNMC, so a declaration of the wrong variant contradicts what is declared and gets the request rejected.

The title tells the two variants apart: the one with connection reads **Declaración responsable del titular del alias sobre la vinculación con registros oficiales**, the one without connection reads **Declaración responsable del titular del alias sin vinculación con registros oficiales**.

**How to fill it in**: the document is in Spanish, it is one page long, and the only parts to complete are the blank lines of the opening paragraph. Everything below that line — the numbered statements and the closing sentence — is already written in the template: do not edit it. That is also where the two variants differ, the one with connection carrying five statements and the one without connection three, which is why the template has to be the right one.

- **Individual templates**: name and surnames of the holder, who signs as a self-employed professional running an economic activity (**titular de actividad económica**), and the **NIF** (or the equivalent tax identification number of the holder country).
- **Company templates**: registered name of the holder, its registered address, its tax identification number, and the name of the legal representative signing for it. These two templates also carry a blank line at the top right of the page: that is the company letterhead, and it has to carry the details of the alias holder, the same ones sent in this request — **aliasHolderName**, then the address made of **holderMailingAddressStreetAvenue**, **holderMailingAddressStreetNumber**, **holderMailingAddressPostalCode**, **holderMailingAddressCity** and **holderMailingAddressCountry**, then the tax identification number **aliasHolderTaxId**, then the contacts **holderEmails** and **holderPhones**. A letterhead carrying a different company than the declared holder contradicts the declaration below it and gets the request rejected. There is an example of it below.
- **Date and signature**: there is no date to write. The holder signs on the blank line at the bottom left of the page with an electronic signature, and the date of that signature is the date of the declaration.

**Example of letterhead, company holder**:

> EJEMPLO COMERCIAL, S.L.
>
> Calle Gran Via, 28, 28013 Madrid, ES
>
> NIF B12345678
>
> info@example.com · +34911234567

**Example, individual holder**. The plain text is the wording already printed in the template: leave it as it is. Only the parts in bold between square brackets are yours to fill in, and the square brackets are not to be typed.

> D./Dña. **[María García López]**, con NIF **[12345678Z]**, titular de actividad económica, declara bajo su responsabilidad:

**Example, company holder**, same convention:

> **[EJEMPLO COMERCIAL, S.L.]**, con domicilio en **[Calle Gran Vía 28, 28013 Madrid]**, y Número de Identificación Fiscal **[B12345678]**, representada por **[Juan Pérez Ruiz]**, mayor de edad, en su calidad de representante legal, declara bajo su responsabilidad:

Both variants of each template open with that same line, so what you write is the same either way: what changes is only the numbered statements printed below it.

The declared name, tax identification number and address must match **aliasHolderName**, **aliasHolderTaxId** and the holder mailing address fields sent in this request, and the holder must be able to produce the supporting documents it declares to have.

Every field is optional: the fields you send are merged over the stored registration data, and the merged result is validated in full against the requirements of the sender's country. Fields you omit keep their current value. Sending a field that is not part of the sender's country requirements has no effect. The sender name, country, type and callback cannot be changed.

aliasHolderType.description: Spain only. Whether the alias holder is a legal entity (**LE**) or a natural person (**NP**). It decides which fields are required: a legal entity declares its registered name in **aliasHolderName** and no surnames, a natural person declares their first name in **aliasHolderName** plus **holder1stSurname**. A sender registered before the alias holder had to be declared has none of these fields stored, so its first correction must carry the whole holder block — this field, **aliasHolderTaxId**, **aliasHolderName**, **holderMailingAddressStreetAvenue**, **holderMailingAddressStreetNumber**, **holderMailingAddressPostalCode**, **holderMailingAddressCity**, **holderMailingAddressCountry**, **holderEmails** and **holderPhones**, plus **holder1stSurname** when the holder is a natural person, or the request will fail.

aliasHolderTaxId.description: Spain only. Tax identification number of the alias holder: the company tax number for a legal entity, the personal one (**NIF**, **NIE** or the equivalent in the holder country) for a natural person. Must match the number in the signed documents.

aliasHolderName.description: Spain only. Registered company name when **aliasHolderType** is **LE**, first name when it is **NP**.

holder1stSurname.description: Spain only. First surname of the alias holder. Required when **aliasHolderType** is **NP**, ignored when it is **LE**.

holder2ndSurname.description: Spain only. Second surname of the alias holder, the Spanish **segundo apellido**. Optional, and only meaningful when **aliasHolderType** is **NP**: leave it out for a holder whose country does not use it.

holderMailingAddressStreetAvenue.description: Spain only. Street name of the alias holder mailing address, without the street number.

holderMailingAddressStreetNumber.description: Spain only. Street number of the alias holder mailing address. For a property with no street number, send the Spanish convention **S/N**.

holderMailingAddressPostalCode.description: Spain only. Postal code of the alias holder mailing address.

holderMailingAddressCity.description: Spain only. City of the alias holder mailing address. It completes the address written on the letterhead of the signed documents, so it must match the address declared in **esLoA** and **esResponsibleDeclaration**.

holderMailingAddressCountry.description: Spain only. Country of the alias holder mailing address, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. It must match the **esLoA** template you signed: a holder in Spain signs the **IB_ES** template, a holder anywhere else signs the **IB_UK** one.

holderEmails.description: Spain only. Contact email address of the alias holder. It is the holder's own address, not the one of its authorised representative, which goes in **representativeEmails**.

holderPhones.description: Spain only. Contact phone number of the alias holder, in E.164 format. It is the holder's own number, not the one of its authorised representative, which goes in **representativePhones**.

holderRepresentativeType.description: Spain only. Whether the authorised representative of the alias holder is a legal entity (**LE**) or a natural person (**NP**). The authorised representative is whoever acts on the alias holder's behalf in the signed documents, typically the natural person who signs them for the holder, and the details declared here must match what is written in those documents. This field decides which of the remaining representative fields are required: a natural person declares **representative1stSurname** and no company block, a legal entity declares its registered name in **representativeName** plus the four **legalEntityRepresentative** fields of the individual acting for it. A sender registered before the authorised representative had to be declared has none of these fields stored, so its first correction must carry the whole representative block — this field, **representativeTaxId**, **representativeName**, **representativeEmails** and **representativePhones**, plus **representative1stSurname** when the representative is a natural person, or **legalEntityRepresentativeTaxId**, **legalEntityRepresentativeName** and **legalEntityRepresentative1stSurname** when it is a legal entity, or the request will fail.

representativeTaxId.description: Spain only. Tax identification number of the authorised representative: the company tax number when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**, the personal one when it is **NP**.

representativeName.description: Spain only. Registered company name of the authorised representative when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**, first name when it is **NP**.

representative1stSurname.description: Spain only. First surname of the authorised representative. Required when **holderRepresentativeType** is **NP**, ignored when it is **LE**.

representative2ndSurname.description: Spain only. Second surname of the authorised representative, the Spanish **segundo apellido**. Optional, and only meaningful when **holderRepresentativeType** is **NP**: leave it out for a representative whose country does not use it.

representativeEmails.description: Spain only. Contact email address of the authorised representative.

representativePhones.description: Spain only. Contact phone number of the authorised representative, in E.164 format.

legalEntityRepresentativeTaxId.description: Spain only. Tax identification number of the individual acting for the authorised representative. Required when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**, ignored when it is **NP**.

legalEntityRepresentativeName.description: Spain only. First name of the individual acting for the authorised representative. Required when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**, ignored when it is **NP**.

legalEntityRepresentative1stSurname.description: Spain only. First surname of the individual acting for the authorised representative. Required when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**, ignored when it is **NP**.

legalEntityRepresentative2ndSurname.description: Spain only. Second surname of the individual acting for the authorised representative. Optional, and only meaningful when **holderRepresentativeType** is **LE**.

Omit it to keep the document already uploaded; send it only to replace that document. The templates are listed in the description of the same field under **POST /senders/alias**.

post.description:
Registers a new alias for a specific destination country, collecting the compliance data required by local regulations and mobile operators.

##### ⚡ Alias registration from the console

You can register and manage your aliases quickly from the [SMS configuration console](https://console.openapi.com/apis/smsv2/configuration).

Every request requires the common fields: **countryCode**, **sender**, **senderCompanyRelationship**, **companyWebsite**, **industry** and **trafficType**. Depending on the selected country, additional fields may be required — select the country schema in the request body to see its specific requirements.

New registrations enter the **PENDING** state and undergo manual review before being submitted to the mobile operators. The review takes **1 to 2 business days** on average; some countries then need further time for the approval by the local mobile operators. In the Sandbox environment (test.sms.openapi.com) new registrations are instead **approved immediately**, without review and without any activation in Production. State transitions (e.g. APPROVED, REJECTED) can be notified asynchronously via the optional **callback**. If the same alias is already registered for the country, the existing registration is returned. Aliases in **DELETED** or **REJECTED** state are the exception: registering them again starts a brand new registration on the same record, billed as a new one, with the registration data sent in the request replacing the previous one.

**IMPORTANT**: the **sender** must clearly refer to your company or to one of its registered brands, and must not be generic: generic aliases (e.g. Info, Alert, Notify, SMS, Verify, Assistenza) are likely to be **rejected** by the reviewers and by the mobile operators. **Use your company or brand name** instead (e.g. Openapi, OpenapiOTP, OpenapiInfo).

patch.description:
Corrects or completes the registration data of a sender in **PATCH_REQUIRED** state — the state a sender is put in when the registration data has to be fixed before it can be approved.

The fields you send are merged over the stored registration data and the merged result is validated in full against the requirements of the sender's country, so omitted fields keep their current value. On success the sender goes back to **PENDING** for review: it cannot send messages until it is approved again. The reason for the correction is available as **patchRequest[0].reason** on GET /senders (**patchRequest** is the history of the correction requests, most recent first).

The sender name, country and registration type cannot be changed. This operation is free of charge.

Only senders in **APPROVED** or **PATCH_REQUIRED** state can be deleted. The registration record is kept for audit purposes.

If the user has an active subscription plan, the message parts will be deducted from the available bundle before charging any remaining balance from the wallet.
